choices.misconception: I treated the powers as multiplication, $2^5 = 2 \cdot 5 = 10$ and $5^3 = 5 \cdot 3 = 15$, so I got $\dfrac{10 \cdot 15}{10} = 15$.
I paired the $2$s with the $5$s to get $10^3 = 1000$ but forgot the two extra $2$s, so I got $1000 \div 10 = 100$.
I worked out $2^5 \cdot 5^3 = 32 \cdot 125 = 4000$ correctly but forgot to divide by $10$.
I got $2^5 \cdot 5^3 = 4000$ but then multiplied by $10$ instead of dividing, so I got $40000$.

hints: Each pair of one $2$ and one $5$ makes a $10$.

solutions.elegant: Three $2$s pair with the three $5$s to make $10^3$, leaving $2^2 = 4$. So the top is $4 \cdot 10^3$, and dividing by $10$ leaves $4 \cdot 10^2 = 400$.
